name_en: Seigaku Mochi — pounded rice cake made without mochi rice
summary_ja: うるち米を粉にせず二度蒸し、臼でついてつくる餅のような料理。高価なもち米を買えない農民にも餅を食べさせたいと、幕末の農民指導者・大原幽学が考えたと伝わり、粘りが少なく喉に詰まりにくいのが特徴。
summary_en: Ordinary non-glutinous rice, steamed twice without grinding and pounded like mochi, makes a rice cake with little of the stickiness of the real thing — said to have been devised by the late-Edo farmer-educator Ohara Yugaku for households that couldn't afford true mochi rice.
source_title: 性学もち 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Gonjuu — pork and fried-tofu rice balls for festival mikoshi bearers
summary_ja: 甘辛く煮た豚バラ肉と油揚げをかつお節とともにご飯に混ぜ、おにぎりにした館山市の郷土料理。秋祭り「やわたんまち」で神輿を担ぐ若衆に振る舞われ、十分に火を通した具が食中毒予防にもなっていたという。
summary_en: Pork belly and fried tofu simmered sweet and savory are mixed with bonito flakes into rice and shaped into onigiri — handed out to the young men carrying the mikoshi at Tateyama's Yawatanmachi festival, the thoroughly cooked filling also said to guard against food poisoning in the late-summer heat.
source_title: ごんじゅう 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Takatsu no Torimeshi — soy-simmered chicken mixed into rice
summary_ja: 小さく切った鶏もも肉を醤油だけで煮て、炊きたてのご飯に混ぜ込む八千代市高津地区の料理。安産祈願の子安講や豊作を願う八朔の行事で食べられてきたと伝わり、肉を小さく切るのは分け合うためとも硬い肉を食べやすくするためとも言われる。
summary_en: Chicken thigh, cut small, is simmered in nothing but soy sauce and mixed into hot rice — a Takatsu district dish said to be served at the koyasu-ko safe-delivery gathering and the hassaku harvest-prayer, the small-cut meat explained either as a way of sharing it fairly or of taming an older bird's tougher meat.
source_title: 高津のとり飯 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Teppou Maki — a katsuobushi rice roll from Futtsu
summary_ja: 炙った海苔にすし飯ではなく普通のご飯を広げ、醤油をかけた鰹節を芯にして巻いた富津市の一品。見た目が鉄砲に似ることが名の由来で、海苔の産地である富津の漁師が携帯食として食べてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Toasted nori is spread not with vinegared sushi rice but with plain rice, rolled around a soy-doused core of bonito flakes — named for its resemblance to a gun barrel, and said to have traveled as portable food for fishermen in Futtsu, a nori-growing town.
source_title: 鉄砲巻き 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Yangome — toasted rice and sweetened azuki for Obon
summary_ja: 一晩水に浸した米を炒り、砂糖で煮た小豆と合わせて蒸らす、赤飯に似た見た目の料理。お盆の迎え火・送り火で唱え言葉とともに米と水をまき、故人を迎え送る行事に結びついた房総半島の食べ物と伝わる。
summary_en: Rice soaked overnight is toasted, then steamed together with azuki beans simmered in sugar — it looks like sekihan but tastes gently sweet, and is tied to the Boso peninsula's Obon custom of scattering rice and water toward the welcoming and send-off fires while chanting for the dead.
source_title: ヤンゴメ 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
